items.stem: What is the difference between concurrency and parallelism?

options.text: Concurrency is structuring work as independent tasks; parallelism is executing tasks literally at the same time on multiple cores
options.rationale: Correct: concurrency is about composition/structure, parallelism about simultaneous execution; you can have one without the other.
They are distinct: concurrent code need not run in parallel, and vice versa.

options.text: Parallelism only works on a single core
options.rationale: Parallelism requires multiple execution units to run simultaneously.
Concurrency is possible on a single core via interleaving.

items.explanation: Correct: concurrency is about composition/structure, parallelism about simultaneous execution; you can have one without the other.

items.stem: Which statements about data races are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: count++ is typically not atomic; it is a read-modify-write that can interleave
options.rationale: Correct: the increment is multiple steps, so concurrent threads can lose updates.

options.text: A data race can be removed by making the operation atomic or guarding it with a lock
options.rationale: Correct: atomics or mutual exclusion restore correctness for shared mutable state.

options.text: Reading a shared variable from many threads while one writes it is always safe
options.rationale: An unsynchronised write with concurrent reads is a data race.

options.text: Data races only occur across separate processes
options.rationale: Data races occur between threads sharing memory within a process.

items.explanation: Correct: the increment is multiple steps, so concurrent threads can lose updates.; Correct: atomics or mutual exclusion restore correctness for shared mutable state.

items.stem: A program is 90% parallelisable and 10% strictly serial. By Amdahl's law, what is the maximum speedup with unlimited cores?

options.rationale: Correct: with the serial fraction s = 0.1, maximum speedup is 1/s = 10x regardless of core count.
The serial 10% caps speedup at 1/0.1 = 10x, not 100x.
The serial fraction bounds speedup; it cannot be unlimited.
Speedup is greater than 1; 0.9x would be a slowdown.

items.explanation: Correct: with the serial fraction s = 0.1, maximum speedup is 1/s = 10x regardless of core count.
